performanceSchema.threadsDescription: View the Performance Schema thread list.
performanceSchema.tableFileIODescription: View table and file I/O statistics.
performanceSchema.rwLocksDescription: View read/write lock ownership and waits.
performanceSchema.metadataLocksDescription: Metadata locks (MDL) protect database object definitions from concurrent changes while queries or transactions use them. Open transactions may hold locks that make ALTER TABLE wait; incompatible pending locks can also affect subsequent access.
performanceSchema.topQueriesDescription: View performance statistics for top SQL queries.

memory.rules: Refresh and compare shows only changed rows. Rates use the total time since the baseline was established. Resetting the baseline only affects this page; it does not clear database statistics or free memory.
memory.comparing: Comparing against a fixed baseline. Repeated refreshes do not move the baseline.
memory.baselineReady: Showing original sample values, saved as the baseline. Click Refresh and compare to see changes.
memory.invalidResponse: The memory API did not return valid JSON. Check the service URL.
memory.precisionError: This browser cannot read this large integer precisely. Upgrade the browser or return strings from the API.
memory.threadPlaceholder: Leave blank for all threads; % and _ wildcards are supported
memory.threadRules: Thread ID is the Performance Schema internal ID, not the process list connection ID. Querying after changing the thread filter establishes a new baseline.
memory.invalidThread: Thread ID may contain only digits and the % and _ wildcards.

metadataLocks.invalidResponse: The metadata lock API did not return JSON. Check the service URL.
metadataLocks.keyword: Filter connections, users, objects, or SQL
metadataLocks.statusHelp: GRANTED means the lock is held; PENDING means it is awaiting grant. State duration is the session time in its current state, not the lock wait time. Lock duration describes statement, transaction, or explicit-release scope, not seconds.

overview.healthDescription: Display most recent performance metrics for all managed servers in a single screen
overview.realtimeTopDescription: View realtime database performance metrics and resource usage rankings.
overview.alerts24hDescription: View database alerts from the last 24 hours.

topQueries.description: Summarize executions, wait times, and resource use by SQL digest, sorted by the selected metric in descending order.
topQueries.rules: The time range filters digests by LAST_SEEN. Metrics remain cumulative, not deltas for the selected period. Timer values are raw picoseconds (1 second = 10¹² ps), memory is in bytes, and fields unavailable in this server version show —.
topQueries.invalidResponse: The top queries API did not return JSON. Check the service URL.
topQueries.precision: This browser cannot read this large integer precisely. Upgrade it or return strings from the API.

digestChanges.title: Changes
digestChanges.noDigest: An empty Digest is an aggregate record and cannot be tracked as an individual digest.
digestChanges.schemaHint: Leave blank for no default schema
digestChanges.rules: Track cumulative metrics for one Schema and Digest. The first query or baseline reset shows raw values. Refresh shows only changed metrics, with rates calculated over the total time since the baseline. Changing the digest requires a new query. Timer values are in picoseconds.
digestChanges.missing: No digest record found. It may not have been collected or may have been cleared or evicted. A new baseline will be established when a record is found.
digestChanges.counterReset: Cumulative counters decreased, possibly after a restart or statistics reset. A new baseline was established automatically.
digestChanges.empty: Select a digest to establish a baseline, or enter Schema and Digest to query.
